Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W) Let me start off by saying I work in freelance video and I love how much I can fit inside this case! I've been using a Pelican 1510 as my go-to travel carrier, so that's mostly what I'm comparing this to. For starters, this is a longer case so in addition to my cameras, lenses, batteries and other accessories, it has a long open sleeve that can even fit a light stand or small tripod! For extra versatility, the whole interior can actually be pulled out (it has its own handle straps if you want to use it as its own carrier), which then frees up the ample storage space inside the case as a separate giant unit (see pictures to illustrate). There are also plenty of pockets on the inside, as well as the outside and front of the case. Of course, for a case this size there is the requisite wheels and carrying handle.
The only things I like better about my Pelican case, however, are the toughness and waterproofing. This bag comes with a rain cover which you can keep inside the case, however I don't like the idea of having to carry around a cover inside the bag, then take it out and put it on if it starts raining. The Pelican cases are air tight by simply closing them, no rain cover needed. The Pelican cases also are tough enough that they can be stacked under other equipment, thrown into a corner, sat on, stood on, etc, and 99% of the time come out unscathed. That's more than I can say for this bag. I bring this bag on gigs that I'm not worried about those things happening, because I can fit what I normally take in 3 separate bags into just this one. You could get a Pelican style case in this size, however it would cost quite a bit more than the asking price of this one. I think for the price this is a great tool to keep your stuff organized and ready to go whenever you are!
text_fidelity_b: Gator Cases 28" Creative Pro Bag for Video Camera Systems with Wheels & Pull Handle (GCPRVCAM28W)

HP 410 Slim Bluetooth Mouse - Bluetooth 5.0, Swift Pair, Blue optical sensor, adjustable up to 1600 DPI tracking, Portable, sleek for Wins PC, Laptop, Notebook, Mac, Work with Chromebook (4M0X5AA#ABL) Since 2010, every time I’ve bought a new laptop, I’ve bought a new wireless mouse. I don’t like using the one on the laptop as it is too awkward and clunky for me.

The mice I prefer – Logitech. The most recent one I got was: Logitech M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top. Though I did get it from Staples (the branding is shortened to Logi).

To me, the brand doesn’t matter – I do try to keep my equipment the same, but the Logitech ones have never let me down. They’re also better shaped for my hand, though the ones of the last decade are smaller, which I LOVE. Last year when I got a new laptop for my birthday, I got the new little Logi listed above.

I saw another HP mouse on here, the HP 930 Creator, and though that would be awesome. It wasn’t. I was quite disappointed. Not that I didn’t like my Logi, I though the HP would be a bit better. And, the 930 was over $67. Many problems, but the main one – size. Far too big for me in height and width.

I saw this and thought it might be better than the 930 – was certainly simpler. I love the FLAT design. It’s about half the height of my Logi.

This, like the 930 has a width problem, thus small hands and those with dexterity issues will have some problems “getting a grip”.

Another issue with this – you need BLUETOOTH capabilities.

Function?

Connection: After turning on my computer’s BLUETOOTH, the mouse connected in under 5 minutes

Sound: A bit quieter than my Logi, as well as the 930 Creator

Scroll: A bit slower than the Logi, definitely slower than the 930

Battery Replacement: Logi – on the bottom, like usual; 930 (rechargeable through USB). This? The battery is on the TOP. You have to remove the top black plate to put the battery in. This is the feature I dislike the most considering how THIN the plastic piece is. Depending on the amount of force used – it could easily get broken.

Currently priced at $39.76, this is definitely a bit overpriced. I am not fond of it, and definitely wouldn’t get a replacement.

UPDATE: As of 3/26, the mouse keeps losing Bluetooth connectivity sometimes in as little as 15 minutes of non-use. I don't know if this is normal with the Bluetooth mouse, but it is definitely annoying especially when I have to reconnect.
text_fidelity_b: HP 410 Slim Bluetooth Mouse - Bluetooth 5.0, Swift Pair, Blue optical sensor, adjustable up to 1600 DPI tracking, Portable, sleek for Wins PC, Laptop, Notebook, Mac, Work with Chromebook (4M0X5AA#ABL)

Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!
text_fidelity_b: Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Carbon Fiber Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders

text_fidelity_a: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black ) This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!
text_fidelity_b: JBL On Tour Portable Speaker System ( Black )

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)
